sanskrit: akārṣīḥ sāhasam idaṃ kasmāt prāyopaveśanam ātmatyāgī hy avāg yāti vācyatāṃ cāyaśaskarīm
english: Why have you undertaken this rash act of sitting in fast unto death? One who abandons himself goes downward and earns reproach and infamy.

sanskrit: na hi kāryaviruddheṣu bahv apāyeṣu karmasu mūlaghātiṣu sajjante buddhimanto bhavadvidhāḥ
english: Wise men of your caliber do not engage in acts that are opposed to purpose, fraught with many dangers, and destructive of all foundations.

sanskrit: niyacchaitāṃ matiṃ rājan dharmārthasukhanāśinīm yaśaḥpratāpadhairyaghnīṃ śatrūṇāṃ harṣavardhanīm
english: Restrain this resolve, O king, which destroys dharma, wealth, and happiness, which ruins fame, valor, and fortitude, and which increases the delight of your enemies.

sanskrit: śrūyatāṃ ca prabho tattvaṃ divyatāṃ cātmano nṛpa nirmāṇaṃ ca śarīrasya tato dhairyam avāpnuhi
english: Hear the truth, O lord; learn of the divine nature of your own self, O king, and of the construction of your body; thereafter you will recover your fortitude.

sanskrit: purā tvaṃ tapasāsmābhir labdho devān maheśvarāt pūrvakāyaś ca sarvas te nirmito vajrasaṃcayaiḥ
english: Long ago you were obtained by us through austerities from the gods and from the great lord Maheśvara; and your entire upper body was fashioned from masses of thunderbolt-substance.

sanskrit: astrair abhedyaḥ śastraiś cāpy adhaḥkāyaś ca te 'nagha kṛtaḥ puṣpamayo devyā rūpataḥ strīmanoharaḥ
english: Your upper body is impenetrable by missiles and weapons, O sinless one; and your lower body was made by the goddess, fashioned of flowers in form, charming to the minds of women.

sanskrit: evam īśvarasaṃyuktas tava deho nṛpottama devyā ca rājaśārdūla divyas tvaṃ hi na mānuṣaḥ
english: Thus your body, O best of kings, O tiger among kings, is joined with the power of the lord and of the goddess — you are divine, not human.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāś ca mahāvīryā bhagadattapurogamāḥ divyāstraviduṣaḥ śūrāḥ kṣapayiṣyanti te ripūn
english: And mighty Kṣatriyas led by Bhagadatta, heroes versed in divine weapons, will annihilate your enemies.

sanskrit: tad alaṃ te viṣādena bhayaṃ tava na vidyate sāhyārthaṃ ca hi te vīrāḥ saṃbhūtā bhuvi dānavāḥ
english: Therefore enough of your despondency — you have nothing to fear; and the heroic Dānavas have taken birth on this earth for the purpose of helping you.

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇakṛpādīṃś ca pravekṣyanty apare 'surāḥ yair āviṣṭā ghṛṇāṃ tyaktvā yotsyante tava vairibhiḥ
english: Other Asuras will enter into Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, and the rest; possessed by them and abandoning all tenderness, they will fight against your enemies.

sanskrit: naiva putrān na ca bhrātṝn na pitṝn na ca bāndhavān naiva śiṣyān na ca jñātīn na bālān sthavirān na ca
english: Neither sons nor brothers, neither fathers nor kinsmen, neither pupils nor relatives, neither children nor aged men —

sanskrit: yudhi saṃprahariṣyanto mokṣyanti kurusattama niḥsnehā dānavāviṣṭāḥ samākrānte 'ntarātmani
english: — will they spare when they strike in battle, O best of Kurus; devoid of affection, possessed by the Dānavas, their inner souls entirely overwhelmed.

sanskrit: prahariṣyanti bandhubhyaḥ sneham utsṛjya dūrataḥ hṛṣṭāḥ puruṣaśārdūlāḥ kaluṣīkṛtamānasāḥ avijñānavimūḍhāś ca daivāc ca vidhinirmitāt
english: Those tiger-like men, casting affection for their kinsmen far away, their minds rendered impure, stupefied by ignorance, and driven by fate and destiny's decree, will strike in gladness.

sanskrit: vyābhāṣamāṇāś cānyonyaṃ na me jīvan vimokṣyase sarvaśastrāstramokṣeṇa pauruṣe samavasthitāḥ ślāghamānāḥ kuruśreṣṭha kariṣyanti janakṣayam
english: Taunting one another — 'You shall not escape me alive' — established in their valor, discharging all weapons and missiles, boasting, O best of Kurus, they shall bring about the destruction of humankind.

sanskrit: te 'pi śaktyā mahātmānaḥ pratiyotsyanti pāṇḍavāḥ vadhaṃ caiṣāṃ kariṣyanti daivayuktā mahābalāḥ
english: The great-souled Pāṇḍavas too, endowed with might and joined with divine force, being of great strength, will fight back against them and will slay them.

sanskrit: daityarakṣogaṇāś cāpi saṃbhūtāḥ kṣatrayoniṣu yotsyanti yudhi vikramya śatrubhis tava pārthiva gadābhir musalaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ śastrair uccāvacais tathā
english: And hosts of Daityas and Rākṣasas born into Kṣatriya wombs will fight with valor against your enemies in battle, O king, with clubs, pestles, swords, and weapons of every description.

sanskrit: yac ca te 'ntargataṃ vīra bhayam arjunasaṃbhavam tatrāpi vihito 'smābhir vadhopāyo 'rjunasya vai
english: And as for the fear of Arjuna that dwells within you, O hero, in that matter too we have arranged a means for the slaying of Arjuna.

sanskrit: hatasya narakasyātmā karṇamūrtim upāśritaḥ tad vairaṃ saṃsmaran vīra yotsyate keśavārjunau
english: The soul of slain Naraka has taken shelter in the form of Karṇa; remembering that old enmity, O hero, he will fight against Keśava and Arjuna.

sanskrit: sa te vikramaśauṇḍīro raṇe pārthaṃ vijeṣyati karṇaḥ praharatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvāṃś cārīn mahārathaḥ
english: That hero, bold in valor — Karṇa, best among warriors, a great chariot-fighter — will conquer Pārtha in battle and defeat all your enemies.

sanskrit: jñātvaitac chadmanā vajrī rakṣārthaṃ savyasācinaḥ kuṇḍale kavacaṃ caiva karṇasyāpahariṣyati
english: Knowing this, Indra the thunderbolt-wielder will, by a stratagem, take away Karṇa's earrings and armor for the sake of protecting Savyasācin (Arjuna).

sanskrit: tasmād asmābhir apy atra daityāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ niyuktā rākṣasāś caiva ye te saṃśaptakā iti prakhyātās te 'rjunaṃ vīraṃ nihaniṣyanti mā śucaḥ
english: Therefore on that account we have appointed hundreds of thousands of Daityas and Rākṣasas here — those who are known as the Saṃśaptakas — they will slay the heroic Arjuna. Grieve not.

sanskrit: asapatnā tvayā hīyaṃ bhoktavyā vasudhā nṛpa mā viṣādaṃ nayasvāsmān naitat tvayy upapadyate vinaṣṭe tvayi cāsmākaṃ pakṣo hīyeta kaurava
english: This earth, freed of rivals, is yours to enjoy, O king; do not lead us into despair — such conduct does not befit you. And if you perish, our own side would be weakened, O Kaurava.

sanskrit: gaccha vīra na te buddhir anyā kāryā kathaṃ cana tvam asmākaṃ gatir nityaṃ devatānāṃ ca pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Go forth, O hero; you must entertain no other thought whatsoever. You are always our refuge — and the Pāṇḍavas are the refuge of the gods.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā pariṣvajya daityās taṃ rājakuñjaram samāśvāsya ca durdharṣaṃ putravad dānavarṣabhāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus and embraced that lion among kings, the foremost of Dānavas consoled the invincible one like a son.

sanskrit: sthirāṃ kṛtvā buddhim asya priyāṇy uktvā ca bhārata gamyatām ity anujñāya jayam āpnuhi cety atha
english: Having steadied his resolve and spoken pleasing words, O Bhārata, they gave him leave saying, 'Go — and may you win victory.'

sanskrit: tair visṛṣṭaṃ mahābāhuṃ kṛtyā saivānayat punaḥ tam eva deśaṃ yatrāsau tadā prāyam upāviśat
english: Released by them, that same Kṛtyā carried the mighty-armed one back again to that very place where he had sat in his fast unto death.

sanskrit: pratinikṣipya taṃ vīraṃ kṛtyā samabhipūjya ca anujñātā ca rājñā sā tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Having set down that hero and duly honored him, the Kṛtyā, dismissed by the king, vanished right there.

sanskrit: gatāyām atha tasyāṃ tu rājā duryodhanas tadā svapnabhūtam idaṃ sarvam acintayata bhārata vijeṣyāmi raṇe pāṇḍūn iti tasyābhavan matiḥ
english: After she had departed, King Duryodhana reflected on all of this as though it had been a dream, O Bhārata; and the thought arose in him: 'I shall conquer the Pāṇḍavas in battle.'

sanskrit: karṇaṃ saṃśaptakāṃś caiva pārthasyāmitraghātinaḥ amanyata vadhe yuktān samarthāṃś ca suyodhanaḥ
english: Suyodhana deemed Karṇa and the Saṃśaptakas, slayers of Pārtha's enemies, to be both suited and capable for killing Arjuna.

sanskrit: evam āśā dṛḍhā tasya dhārtarāṣṭrasya durmateḥ vinirjaye pāṇḍavānām abhavad bharatarṣabha
english: Thus a firm hope for defeating the Pāṇḍavas arose in that evil-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: karṇo 'py āviṣṭacittātmā narakasyāntarātmanā arjunasya vadhe krūrām akarot sa matiṃ tadā
english: And Karṇa too, his mind and soul possessed by Naraka's inner spirit, then formed a cruel resolve for the slaying of Arjuna.

sanskrit: saṃśaptakāś ca te vīrā rākṣasāviṣṭacetasaḥ rajastamobhyām ākrāntāḥ phalgunasya vadhaiṣiṇaḥ
english: And those heroic Saṃśaptakas, their minds possessed by Rākṣasas, overwhelmed by passion and darkness, became seekers of Phalguna's (Arjuna's) death.

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇakṛpādyāś ca dānavākrāntacetasaḥ na tathā pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ snehavanto viśāṃ pate na cācacakṣe kasmai cid etad rājā suyodhanaḥ
english: And Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, and the others, their hearts seized by Dānavas, were no longer so affectionate toward the sons of Pāṇḍu, O lord of the people. And King Suyodhana disclosed none of this to anyone.

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ niśānte ca karṇo vaikartano 'bravīt smayann ivāñjaliṃ kṛtvā pārthivaṃ hetumad vacaḥ
english: At the close of night Karṇa Vaikartana addressed Duryodhana, joining his palms with a slight smile, speaking reasoned words to the king.

sanskrit: na mṛto jayate śatrūñ jīvan bhadrāṇi paśyati mṛtasya bhadrāṇi kutaḥ kauraveya kuto jayaḥ na kālo 'dya viṣādasya bhayasya maraṇasya vā
english: 'The dead man does not conquer enemies; the living man sees prosperity. Where is prosperity for the dead, O son of Kuru — where is victory? Today is no time for despondency, for fear, or for death.'

sanskrit: pariṣvajyābravīc cainaṃ bhujābhyāṃ sa mahābhujaḥ uttiṣṭha rājan kiṃ śeṣe kasmāc chocasi śatruhan śatrūn pratāpya vīryeṇa sa kathaṃ martum icchasi
english: The mighty-armed one embraced him with both arms and said: 'Arise, O king — why do you lie there? Why do you grieve, O slayer of enemies? You who have scorched your foes with your valor — how can you wish to die?'

sanskrit: atha vā te bhayaṃ jātaṃ dṛṣṭvārjunaparākramam satyaṃ te pratijānāmi vadhiṣyāmi raṇe 'rjunam
english: 'Or if fear has arisen in you upon seeing Arjuna's valor, I swear to you truly: I will slay Arjuna in battle.'

sanskrit: gate trayodaśe varṣe satyenāyudham ālabhe ānayiṣyāmy ahaṃ pārthān vaśaṃ tava janādhipa
english: 'When the thirteenth year has passed, I take up my weapon in earnest — I will bring the Pārthas under your dominion, O lord of the people.'

sanskrit: evam uktas tu karṇena daityānāṃ vacanāt tathā praṇipātena cānyeṣām udatiṣṭhat suyodhanaḥ daityānāṃ tad vacaḥ śrutvā hṛdi kṛtvā sthirāṃ matim
english: Thus addressed by Karṇa, and likewise by the words of the Daityas and the prostrations of others, Suyodhana rose up; having heard the words of the Daityas, he fixed a firm resolve in his heart.

sanskrit: tato manujaśārdūlo yojayām āsa vāhinīm rathanāgāśvakalilāṃ padātijanasaṃkulām
english: Then that tiger among men marshaled his army — dense with chariots, elephants, and horses, and thronging with infantry.

sanskrit: gaṅgaughapratimā rājan prayātā sā mahācamūḥ śvetacchatraiḥ patākābhiś cāmaraiś ca supāṇḍuraiḥ
english: That great army set forth, O king, resembling the flood of the Gaṅgā, gleaming with white parasols, banners, and bright white fly-whisks.

sanskrit: rathair nāgaiḥ padātaiś ca śuśubhe 'tīva saṃkulā vyapetābhraghane kāle dyaur ivāvyaktaśāradī
english: Exceedingly crowded with chariots, elephants, and foot-soldiers, it shone brilliantly — like the autumnal sky, indistinct yet clear, when the thick clouds have passed away.

sanskrit: jayāśīrbhir dvijendrais tu stūyamāno 'dhirājavat gṛhṇann añjalimālāś ca dhārtarāṣṭro janādhipaḥ
english: Praised with victory-blessings by the foremost Brahmins as though he were a paramount sovereign, and receiving garlands of joined palms, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the people —

sanskrit: suyodhano yayāv agre śriyā paramayā jvalan karṇena sārdhaṃ rājendra saubalena ca devinā
english: — Suyodhana marched at the fore, blazing with supreme splendor, together with Karṇa and Saubala the gambler, O lord of kings.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanādayaś cāsya bhrātaraḥ sarva eva te bhūriśravāḥ somadatto mahārājaś ca bāhlikaḥ
english: And all his brothers headed by Duḥśāsana, and Bhūriśravas, Somadatta, and the great king Bāhlika —

sanskrit: rathair nānāvidhākārair hayair gajavarais tathā prayāntaṃ nṛpasiṃhaṃ tam anujagmuḥ kurūdvahāḥ kālenālpena rājaṃs te viviśuḥ svapuraṃ tadā
english: — the foremost of Kurus followed that lion among kings as he marched, in chariots of varied forms, with horses and excellent elephants; and in a short time, O king, they all entered their own city.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca vasamāneṣu pārtheṣu vane tasmin mahātmasu dhārtarāṣṭrā maheṣvāsāḥ kim akurvanta sattama
english: Janamejaya said: While the great-souled Pārthas were dwelling in that forest, what did the Dhārtarāṣṭras, those great bowmen, do, O virtuous one?

sanskrit: karṇo vaikartanaś cāpi śakuniś ca mahābalaḥ bhīṣmadroṇakṛpāś caiva tan me śaṃsitum arhasi
english: Karṇa Vaikartana, the mighty Śakuni, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and Kṛpa — please relate all of this to me.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ gateṣu pārtheṣu visṛṣṭe ca suyodhane āgate hāstinapuraṃ mokṣite pāṇḍunandanaiḥ bhīṣmo 'bravīn mahārāja dhārtarāṣṭram idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: After the Pārthas had gone away thus, and Suyodhana had been released and arrived at Hāstinapura, freed by the sons of Pāṇḍu, Bhīṣma spoke these words to the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O great king.

sanskrit: uktaṃ tāta mayā pūrvaṃ gacchatas te tapovanam gamanaṃ me na rucitaṃ tava tan na kṛtaṃ ca te
english: 'It was said by me before, dear child, when you were setting out for the forest-hermitage — that expedition did not please me; yet you did not do as I said.'

sanskrit: tataḥ prāptaṃ tvayā vīra grahaṇaṃ śatrubhir balāt mokṣitaś cāsi dharmajñaiḥ pāṇḍavair na ca lajjase
english: 'Then, O hero, you suffered capture by your enemies by force; and you were released by the Pāṇḍavas who know dharma — and yet you feel no shame.'

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ tava gāndhāre sasainyasya viśāṃ pate sūtaputro 'payād bhīto gandharvāṇāṃ tadā raṇāt krośatas tava rājendra sasainyasya nṛpātmaja
english: 'It was witnessed by you yourself, O scion of Gāndhāra, O lord of the people, that the charioteer's son fled in fear from the battle against the Gandharvas while you, O lord of kings, O son of a king, were crying out for help along with your army.'

sanskrit: dṛṣṭas te vikramaś caiva pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām karṇasya ca mahābāho sūtaputrasya durmateḥ
english: 'The valor of the great-souled Pāṇḍavas has been seen by you, O mighty-armed one, as well as that of Karṇa the charioteer's son of wicked mind.'

sanskrit: na cāpi pādabhāk karṇaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ nṛpottama dhanurvede ca śaurye ca dharme vā dharmavatsala
english: 'Nor is Karṇa worthy to be even at the feet of the Pāṇḍavas, O best of kings — not in archery, not in valor, not in dharma, O you who love dharma.'

sanskrit: tasya te 'haṃ kṣamaṃ manye pāṇḍavais tair mahātmabhiḥ saṃdhiṃ saṃdhividāṃ śreṣṭha kulasyāsya vivṛddhaye
english: 'For this reason I consider it proper for you to make peace with those great-souled Pāṇḍavas, O best of those who know the art of reconciliation, for the prosperity of this lineage.'

sanskrit: evam uktas tu bhīṣmeṇa dhārtarāṣṭro janeśvaraḥ prahasya sahasā rājan vipratasthe sasaubalaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Bhīṣma, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the people, suddenly laughed and departed with Saubala, O king.

sanskrit: taṃ tu prasthitam ājñāya karṇaduḥśāsanādayaḥ anujagmur maheṣvāsā dhārtarāṣṭraṃ mahābalam
english: Knowing him to have set forth, Karṇa, Duḥśāsana, and the others — great bowmen — followed behind the mighty son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu saṃprasthitān dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ lajjayā vrīḍito rājañ jagāma svaṃ niveśanam
english: Seeing them depart thus, Bhīṣma the grandsire of the Kurus, ashamed and abashed, O king, went to his own quarters.

sanskrit: gate bhīṣme mahārāja dhārtarāṣṭro janādhipaḥ punar āgamya taṃ deśam amantrayata mantribhiḥ
english: After Bhīṣma had departed, O great king, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the people, returned to that place and consulted with his ministers.

sanskrit: kim asmākaṃ bhavec chreyaḥ kiṃ kāryam avaśiṣyate kathaṃ nu sukṛtaṃ ca syān mantrayām āsa bhārata
english: 'What would be to our benefit? What task remains to be done? How might something well accomplished come about?' — thus he took counsel, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca duryodhana nibodhedaṃ yat tvā vakṣyāmi kaurava śrutvā ca tat tathā sarvaṃ kartum arhasy ariṃdama
english: Karṇa said: Duryodhana, hear this that I shall tell you, O Kaurava; and having heard it, you ought to do exactly all of it, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: tavādya pṛthivī vīra niḥsapatnā nṛpottama tāṃ pālaya yathā śakro hataśatrur mahāmanāḥ
english: 'Today the earth is yours without rival, O hero, O best of kings; rule it as Indra, the great-minded slayer of his enemies, rules his realm.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu karṇena karṇaṃ rājābravīt punaḥ na kiṃ cid durlabhaṃ tasya yasya tvaṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Karṇa, the king again spoke to Karṇa: 'Nothing is unattainable for him who has you, O bull among men.'

sanskrit: sahāyaś cānuraktaś ca madarthaṃ ca samudyataḥ abhiprāyas tu me kaś cit taṃ vai śṛṇu yathātatham
english: 'You are my ally, devoted to me, and ever ready for my sake. But I have a certain desire — hear it truly as it is.'

sanskrit: rājasūyaṃ pāṇḍavasya dṛṣṭvā kratuvaraṃ tadā mama spṛhā samutpannā tāṃ saṃpādaya sūtaja
english: 'Having witnessed the Pāṇḍava's Rājasūya sacrifice, that chief of rituals, a longing arose in me then — fulfill it, O son of a charioteer.'

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ karṇo rājānam idam abravīt tavādya pṛthivīpālā vaśyāḥ sarve nṛpottama
english: Thus addressed, Karṇa then said this to the king: 'Today all the guardians of the earth are subject to you, O best of kings.'

sanskrit: āhūyantāṃ dvijavarāḥ saṃbhārāś ca yathāvidhi saṃbhriyantāṃ kuruśreṣṭha yajñopakaraṇāni ca
english: 'Let the foremost Brahmins be summoned; let the materials be gathered properly; let the implements of sacrifice be assembled, O best of Kurus.'

sanskrit: ṛtvijaś ca samāhūtā yathoktaṃ vedapāragāḥ kriyāṃ kurvantu te rājan yathāśāstram ariṃdama
english: 'And let the officiating priests be called together — those versed in the Vedas as prescribed — let them perform the rites for you, O king, according to scripture, O subduer of foes.'

sanskrit: bahvannapānasaṃyuktaḥ susamṛddhaguṇānvitaḥ pravartatāṃ mahāyajñas tavāpi bharatarṣabha
english: 'Let a great sacrifice, furnished with abundant food and drink, endowed with fully flourishing qualities, be undertaken for you as well, O bull of the Bharatas.'

sanskrit: evam uktas tu karṇena dhārtarāṣṭro viśāṃ pate purohitaṃ samānāyya idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by Karṇa, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O lord of the people, summoned his household priest and spoke these words.

sanskrit: rājasūyaṃ kratuśreṣṭhaṃ samāptavaradakṣiṇam āhara tvaṃ mama kṛte yathānyāyaṃ yathākramam
english: 'Conduct the Rājasūya, the foremost of sacrifices, complete with its excellent fees, for my sake, in proper order and due sequence.'

sanskrit: sa evam ukto nṛpatim uvāca dvijapuṃgavaḥ na sa śakyaḥ kratuśreṣṭho jīvamāne yudhiṣṭhire āhartuṃ kauravaśreṣṭha kule tava nṛpottama
english: Thus addressed, that foremost of twice-born men said to the king: 'That foremost of sacrifices cannot be conducted while Yudhiṣṭhira lives, O best of Kauravas, O best of kings in your lineage.'

sanskrit: dīrghāyur jīvati ca vai dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ pitā tava ataś cāpi viruddhas te kratur eṣa nṛpottama
english: 'Moreover, your father Dhṛtarāṣṭra lives and is long-lived; and for that reason too this sacrifice is barred to you, O best of kings.'

sanskrit: asti tv anyan mahat satraṃ rājasūyasamaṃ prabho tena tvaṃ yaja rājendra śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: 'There is, however, another great sacrifice equal to the Rājasūya, O lord; with that, do you sacrifice, O king of kings — and hear this word of mine.'

sanskrit: ya ime pṛthivīpālāḥ karadās tava pārthiva te karān saṃprayacchantu suvarṇaṃ ca kṛtākṛtam
english: 'Let these guardians of the earth who are your tributaries, O king, present their tributes and gold both wrought and unwrought.'

sanskrit: tena te kriyatām adya lāṅgalaṃ nṛpasattama yajñavāṭasya te bhūmiḥ kṛṣyatāṃ tena bhārata
english: 'With that, let a plough be made for you today, O best of kings; and let the ground of your sacrificial enclosure be tilled with it, O Bhārata.'

sanskrit: tatra yajño nṛpaśreṣṭha prabhūtānnaḥ susaṃskṛtaḥ pravartatāṃ yathānyāyaṃ sarvato hy anivāritaḥ
english: 'There, O best of kings, let a sacrifice well performed, abundantly stocked with food, proceed in proper order, unobstructed from all sides.'

sanskrit: eṣa te vaiṣṇavo nāma yajñaḥ satpuruṣocitaḥ etena neṣṭavān kaś cid ṛte viṣṇuṃ purātanam
english: 'This is called the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice for you — fit for righteous men; none but ancient Viṣṇu has ever performed this.'

sanskrit: rājasūyaṃ kratuśreṣṭhaṃ spardhaty eṣa mahākratuḥ asmākaṃ rocate caiva śreyaś ca tava bhārata avighnaś ca bhaved eṣa saphalā syāt spṛhā tava
english: 'This great sacrifice rivals the Rājasūya, the foremost of rites; it is pleasing to us and will be to your benefit, O Bhārata; and it will proceed without obstacle, so that your desire may bear fruit.'

sanskrit: evam uktas tu tair viprair dhārtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ karṇaṃ ca saubalaṃ caiva bhrātṝṃś caivedam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by those Brahmins, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the earth, then spoke these words to Karṇa, Saubala, and his brothers.
